**Move to Node.js 26.13.1.**

The container image and CI move to Node.js 26.13.1, the current Active LTS line, and the server now requires Node.js 26.13.1 or later. Native installs must upgrade Node.js before they update to this release.

## Changed

- **Run on Node.js 26.13.1** — The container image installs Node.js from the `nodejs-26` package, 26.13.1 or later, on the 2026-11-20 `cgr.dev/chainguard/wolfi-base` digest. The server refuses to start on a Node.js release earlier than 26.13.1, including ever

**Check every name an archive entry can be extracted under, and pool connections to S3 storage again.**

Upload inspection now checks each name an extractor may give an archive entry, including a ZIP entry's raw name field when its Unicode Path field names it differently, and a tar entry's GNU long name. The vendored framework moves to blamejs 0.21.8, and connections to the configured S3 storage are pooled again, which removes the extra TLS handshake per request that v1.15.12 introduced.

`scripts/vault-key-rotate.js` stopped with `FATAL: invalid tag` on every database a running server had written, and `scripts/vault-key-verify.js` reported a healthy database as `db.key.enc is corrupted`. Neither tool changed any data, but the messages read as a damaged database. Both tools now read the database the way the server does. The rotation also no longer renames the data directory, so it runs when `/app/data` is a Docker volume, and the offline vault tools now detect a running server from the data

**Move to Node.js 24.22.1 for the CVE-2026-111497 Brotli decoder fix.**

Node.js 24.22.1 fixes CVE-2026-111497, an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder bundled with Node.js that malformed compressed data can trigger, and seven other vulnerabilities in DNS, TLS, HTTP, crypto and the Permission Model. The container image now refuses to build with an older Node, and the server refuses to start on one.

## Security

- **Run on Node.js 24.22.1** — The container image installs `nodejs-24` 24.22.1 or newer

A Local → S3 storage migration on v1.15.9 could replace a file with an empty object after a transient error from the storage service and then delete the local copy. If you ran one, read the Migration section. This release also stops S3 uploads and downloads from holding their data in memory for two minutes after they finish, reports a damaged vault.key.sealed as a damaged file rather than a rejected passphrase, converts the database so that the daily vacuum frees pages, makes the TLS listener choose the s

**Ship the session, password-check and log fixes that v1.15.8 could not publish.**

v1.15.8 was tagged but produced no image and no release page. blamejs 0.20.39 was published after that release was prepared, and the build's check that the vendored framework is the latest release refused it. Use this version instead. It carries every v1.15.8 change with blamejs 0.20.39. Read the v1.15.8 entry in CHANGELOG.md before you upgrade from 1.15.7 or earlier: it lists changes to log fields, to the bundle init routes

**Uploaded SVGs are checked for a link hidden behind a namespace prefix.**

A framework refresh whose one change reaching this server is in the SVG guard. Nothing in your configuration changes and there is no migration. The desktop sync client moves to the same framework version in its own release, and the two were tested together end to end before either was tagged.

**The v1.15.4 container could not start; this release fixes it.**

The v1.15.4 image exits immediately with a dynamic linker error and never serves a request. If you pull `latest`, `1`, `1.15` or `1.15.4`, take this release instead. Nothing in your configuration or data is affected, and there is no migration. Deployments that run from source rather than the container image were never affected.
